```{python}
import palmerpenguins
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
```

## Get Data

Load the Palmer Penguins data and retain observations with complete values for the model outcome and predictors.

```{python}
df = palmerpenguins.load_penguins()

model_columns = [
    "bill_length_mm",
    "species",
    "sex",
    "body_mass_g",
]

model_df = df.dropna(subset=model_columns)
retained_n = len(model_df)
excluded_n = len(df) - len(model_df)
```

The model retains `{python} retained_n` of `{python} len(df)` observations and
excludes `{python} excluded_n` observations with missing values in the model
outcome or predictors.

## Define Model and Fit

Fit a linear regression predicting body mass from bill length, species, and sex. Categorical predictors are converted to indicator variables.

```{python}
X = pd.get_dummies(model_df[["bill_length_mm", "species", "sex"]], drop_first=True)
y = model_df["body_mass_g"]

model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
```

## Model Evaluation

The output provides basic checks that the model ran successfully. The reported R-square describes fit to the training data, not performance on new observations.

```{python}
print(f"Training R^2 {model.score(X, y)}")
print(f"Intercept {model.intercept_}")
print(f"Columns {X.columns}")
print(f"Coefficients {model.coef_}")
```
